summary: Frontend-only regression completed on public URL. Mobile 390 long-run East-West perimeter now advances continuously across 30s+ and survives blur/scroll/pagehide/pageshow recovery. 66-page chrome contract and favicon rollout validated via new reusable pytest; legacy lang-toggle tests still fail due outdated assumptions.

integration_issues.issue: Existing tests in test_lang_switch_overlay_order.py and test_lang_toggle_regression.py assert outdated menu/header language-switch structure and brittle snippet parsing, producing false failures against approved new contract.

action_items: Resolved: DOM-aware overlay/order tests now expect exactly one header switch and zero side-menu switches.

Resolved: language/guard tests compare original header links and PRE-change body/head hashes outside explicitly approved chrome/favicon scope, rather than blindly refreshing full-page expected hashes.
Physical iOS Safari/Android validation is still pending; this run used emulated Chromium + CDP touch, not a physical device.
critical_code_review_comments: east-west-feature.js correctly removed blur-gated dependency and uses infinite WAAPI iterations with one timed slideshow callback per cycle.
styles.css is very large (>700 lines), which increases regression risk; modularization recommended in a separate refactor.
Language-switch contract is consistent in current source: exactly one header switch per page and zero side-menu switches across all 66 pages.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Dynamic checks done on public URL at 390 and 1920. Mobile 390: EW border lines are 3px and glint 5px; slide index advanced every ~5.2s over 6 cycles; WAAPI currentTime advanced across blur+scroll and resumed after pagehide/pageshow. Desktop 1920: hover pauses EW animation and pointerleave resumes; side-menu has no lang switch and header keeps one. CDP touch emulation (Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled + Input.dispatchTouchEvent) opened side menu successfully. New reusable test file /app/tests/test_iter68_frontend_contract.py passes 6/6 and validates 66-page content parity + favicon links + language switch placement.
rca of the issue: The 5 initial legacy failures were outdated test expectations and attribute-order parsing. Those tests were aligned with the user's approved chrome/favicon scope and re-run successfully; the real mobile freeze was separately reproduced before changes as a blur/focus gate leaving visible animations paused.
